Population die-off on a negative-hab world looks far too harsh: Kochab lost 100 of 800 colonists in one year at only -1% habitability (12.5%/yr). In the original game a -1% world decays at a fraction of a percent per year.

Negative-hab colonies are unrecoverable by design: resources = pop/1000 + factories truncates to 0 below 1000 pop, and the factory/mine cap is also 0, so such a planet can NEVER build a TERRAFORM item to repair its own habitability. Biotechnology is therefore useless for rescuing exactly the colonies terraforming exists to rescue.

Fuel appears to be computed as mass x distance x 0.005 x warp with no engine-efficiency term. Consequence: the Propulsion field has zero effect on range or fuel use, and range scales as 1/warp, so warp 1-2 travel is nearly free (a 42 kT ship with 150 fuel could cross 357 ly at warp 2). The original game gives each engine a per-warp fuel curve; this looks like a port omission.

Long Range Scout #10 has reported riding out a galactic storm and taking hull damage for two consecutive years while sitting at (340,205) with onward movement orders queued - the fleet does not appear able to leave the storm. Possible stuck-fleet bug, or at least no visible escape mechanic.

When a fleet exhausts fuel the engine sets warp 0 and leaves it there permanently. Later orders then spend both the energy and the very minerals the blocked order is waiting for, which can starve it forever. The code comment at 500-503 admits the deviation: C# FactoryProductionUnit.cs banks per-resource RemainingCost with proportional mineral spend, the web model makes minerals all-or-nothing.
